canonical_name: Symmetry of the Green function of a self-adjoint operator
canonical_statement: Let H be a complex Hilbert space and A a densely defined self-adjoint operator on H with zero in its resolvent set. Its Green operator G = A^{-1} is bounded and self-adjoint. Whenever G is represented by an integral kernel K relative to a fixed measure and the representation determines K almost everywhere, K(x,y) equals the complex conjugate of K(y,x) almost everywhere. In the real-valued case this is symmetry K(x,y)=K(y,x).
domain_and_universes: A complex Hilbert space H; a densely defined self-adjoint (possibly unbounded) operator A; its bounded inverse G; a measure space used only for the optional kernel corollary.
quantifiers: A : densely defined self-adjoint operator on H
h0 : 0 belongs to the resolvent set of A
G : bounded operator H -> H with G = A^{-1}
optional kernel data (X, mu, K) representing G
hypotheses: A is densely defined and self-adjoint
0 is in the resolvent set, so the everywhere-defined inverse is bounded
for the kernel conclusion, K represents G and the chosen representation has an almost-everywhere uniqueness theorem
conclusion: G is self-adjoint; consequently a representing kernel is Hermitian almost everywhere, and symmetric almost everywhere when real-valued.

alternate_encodings.target: For a bounded invertible self-adjoint operator A, the continuous-linear inverse A^{-1} is self-adjoint

excluded_degenerate_cases: Zero modes are excluded by the resolvent hypothesis. Generalized Green functions, non-self-adjoint operators, distributional kernels without an a.e. function representative, pointwise equality without regularity, and unspecified boundary conditions are outside this root.
